verdict_reason: The start-up, Nunjucks root, fixture-sharing and Joi updates match the code, but the stylesheet paragraph describes a copied _sub-navigation.scss that does not exist.

todos.issue: Lines 128-135 say 'The MoJ sub navigation stylesheet is copied to _sub-navigation.scss rather than imported from @ministryofjustice/frontend' because of a Sass 'already loaded' conflict. No _sub-navigation.scss exists under src/client/stylesheets/. The code does the opposite: application.scss:2 imports it from the package (@use "@ministryofjustice/frontend/moj/components/sub-navigation/sub-navigation"), and _govuk-frontend.scss:1 configures MoJ's vendored govuk-frontend with $moj-assets-path and $govuk-global-styles, then forwards pkg:govuk-frontend. A reader following the doc would look for, or recreate, a copied stylesheet that is not there.
todos.fix: Must: the build paragraph describes how the stylesheets are wired at this commit: _govuk-frontend.scss configures GOV.UK Frontend through @ministryofjustice/frontend's vendored copy ($moj-assets-path, $govuk-global-styles) and forwards pkg:govuk-frontend, and application.scss uses the package's sub-navigation component directly. If the Sass conflict is the reason for routing through the MoJ vendor module, it says that, not a copy. One way: replace the copy sentence with 'application.scss uses the MoJ sub navigation component from the package. _govuk-frontend.scss configures GOV.UK Frontend through MoJ's vendored module, because configuring pkg:govuk-frontend directly and then loading the MoJ component fails with "This module was already loaded..."'.
